Frontier ECI and the benchmark scores behind it

Coloured lines are the benchmark scores of the 22 models that set a new frontier ECI from GPT-4 onward (named along the top), in log-odds (left axis). Colour shows each benchmark's area; tap an area to isolate it. The thick line is frontier ECI itself (right axis), with its 90% interval.

The interactive chart could not load here, so this is the static version.

Data: Epoch AI's own ECI fit input (processed_data_for_eci.csv) and published ECI scores (eci_scores.csv) from benchmark_data.zip, snapshot of 1 Oct 2026, shown from GPT-4 (14 Mar 2023) onward. Every score is already floor- and ceiling-adjusted: (raw − random-guess baseline) ÷ (attainable ceiling − baseline), clipped to [0, 1], taking the best version within each model group. Frontier ECI is the running maximum by release date; where several models share a date only the highest counts. The 22 record-setting models contribute of the scores shown, on 49 of the 60 benchmarks. Their ECIs still depend on the whole joint fit, including the few pre-GPT-4 models not shown.

Areas follow the primary domain tag on Epoch's ECI page, grouped into seven: Math; Software engineering (includes Cybench); Agents & computer use; Science; Reasoning & games (conceptual reasoning plus games); Multimodal; Language & knowledge (language understanding, world knowledge, long context, writing). Seven benchmarks have no tag there and were assigned by hand: METR Time Horizons, DeepResearch Bench (agents), LMCA (reasoning), Lech Mazur Writing (language), GeoBench (multimodal), and the two FrontierMath v1 sets (math).

Solid vertical lines mark the start of each year; dotted lines mark the release of each frontier model. The slope-matched right axis is scaled so a benchmark with the median fitted slope (0.107 logits per ECI point) runs parallel to the ECI line; steeper benchmarks climb faster than it. Scores of exactly 0 or 1 are pinned to 1% and 99%. Data CC BY 4.0, Epoch AI.
